headlines.title: Two researchers who left Anthropic and Google warn AI could become ‘uncontrollable’
headlines.description: After Jacob Coxon roiled the AI industry with his viral departure from Anthropic, two more researchers are speaking out about their concerns over AI safety.

headlines.title: Florida attorney general sues Netflix over ‘bait-and-switch’ on privacy for kids
headlines.description: Florida’s attorney general filed a sweeping lawsuit against Netflix, accusing the streaming giant of misleading consumers about its data collection practices.

headlines.title: China hits back at U.S. claim its AI companies systematically copied American models
headlines.description: In its most detailed accusation yet, the U.S. government has named six Chinese AI companies that it says copied American companies for their AI secrets.

headlines.title: ‘Never Forget’: How Americans remember Sept. 11
headlines.description: From an 11-year-old watching the towers fall on a classroom TV to a doctor treating victims in a conference room, NBC News readers share their searing memories from Sept. 11, 2001.

headlines.title: Hillary Clinton warns the U.S. has let its guard down on terrorism 25 years after 9/11
headlines.description: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton warned Thursday that the Trump administration isn’t doing enough to monitor and thwart terrorists who still pose a threat to the U.S., 25 years after the 9/11 attacks.

headlines.title: More AI researchers warn of AI's threat to humanity
headlines.description: NBC News' Tom Llamas spoke to two more artificial intelligence researchers about the potential threat A.I has to humanity. This comes after AI researcher Jacob Coxon shared a viral tweet saying he believed AI could kill humanity in the next decade. Llamas also spoke to Incoming Professor at UC Berkley Sayash Kapoor who also warns of risk, but says policy proposals and regulations can help prevent further threats.

headlines.title: Growing chorus of A.I. insiders warns of possible extinction of humans
headlines.description: Former employees from some of the top A.I. companies say the potential of future models is nothing short of the killing of all humans. NBC News’ Christine Romans reports.

headlines.title: Apple Unveils New Foldable Device iPhone Duo, 18Pro Models
headlines.description: Apple revealed the new iPhone Duo, a folding phone that is now the company’s most expensive ever made. The keynote was the first led by the company’s new CEO John Ternus after he officially took the reins from Tim Cook. NBC’s Savannah Sellers reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Anthropic Researcher's Apocalyptic Warning on AI Sets Off Debate
headlines.description: A researcher at Anthropic resigned and shared a chilling warning that AI models pose a risk of taking over the world within six months. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” he wrote, adding, “Neither company is acting responsibly.” Now, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are calling for more scrutiny. NBC’s Christine Romans reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: AI researcher says there is 'substantial probability' AI could kill all humans in next decade
headlines.description: Former AI researcher for Anthropic and Open AI, Jacob Coxon, talked to NBC News' Tom Llamas about his viral tweet where he stated AI could "kill us all" by the end of the next decade. Coxon spoke about why he resigned from Anthropic, how AI advancements are creating major concerns and what could be done about it.

headlines.title: Critics say ‘fashion slop’ is coming for the industry’s design creativity
headlines.description: As social media makes trends move faster than ever, some fashion brands are leaning into A.I. and algorithms to churn out more clothes some are calling "slop." NBC News’ Yasmin Vossoughian reports.

headlines.title: Apple unveils foldable iPhone
headlines.description: NBC News’ Savannah Sellers reports from Cupertino, CA where Apple’s new CEO debuted the company’s first foldable iPhone. Savannah was one of the first people to get a chance to try out the new device.
